task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 31, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer answering how the Wren Coast hotel group's occupancy rate increased while it sold fewer room nights and took in less room revenue.

facts.text: The Wren Coast Lodging Association's August 2026 report compares the same five participating hotels in April 2025 and April 2026.
The hotels offered 3,000 available room nights in April 2025 and sold 2,400, an occupancy rate of 80%.
Renovations removed 20 rooms from service for all 30 days of April 2026, reducing available room nights to 2,400.
The hotels sold 2,040 room nights in April 2026, producing an occupancy rate of 85%.
Sold room nights fell by 360, or 15%, even as occupancy rose by five percentage points.
Across the five hotels, room revenue divided by sold room nights was $100 in April 2025 and $110 in April 2026, the report's average daily room rates.
Room revenue was $240,000 in the earlier month and $224,400 in the later month, a 6.5% decrease.
Room revenue per available room night rose from $80 to $93.50 because the available inventory changed.
Room nights are not individual guests: one room may hold more than one person and one stay may last several nights.
The revenue totals exclude food, parking and event income, and they do not measure profit.
Association analyst Ceri Venn said a higher occupancy rate can describe fuller remaining capacity rather than more total business.
Venn said, "A smaller hotel can look fuller on the percentage line while its reception desk sells fewer nights."
The renovations affected room types unevenly, so the higher average rate does not establish that every room's listed price increased by 10%.
Restaurant owner Tavin Holt says hotel guests are one source of customers, alongside local residents and day visitors.
Holt said, "I cannot turn a hotel percentage into a count of people coming through my door."
The association's five hotels are voluntary reporting members, not every lodging business on the coast.
Short-term rentals and campsites are outside the report.
The report does not isolate changes caused by renovations, demand, prices or the mix of rooms sold.
Two participating hotels occupy converted boardinghouses, while the other three were purpose-built.
The association expects the renovated rooms to return to sale in autumn but has not published confirmed opening dates.

forbidden_additions: Higher occupancy proves more visitors or greater total room revenue
Room revenue is profit, all room prices rose uniformly or the sample covers all tourism
preserve: If quoted: A smaller hotel can look fuller on the percentage line while its reception desk sells fewer nights.

Inventory, sold room nights, occupancy and revenue are distinct measures.
